function: Joint learning of the probing-beam pattern and prediction of the optimal transmit-receive beam pair from RSRP of probing beam pairs, for mmWave beam management (p. 3-4).
system: mmWave downlink, single-cell indoor factory at 30 GHz (FR2); BS 4x8 UPA with 32 beams, UE 1x4 array with 4 beams; no RIS (p. 8, Table I).
method: Supervised end-to-end network: sampling network (modified Sigmoid, learnable matrix) selects probing beams, CNN plus self-attention network predicts the beam; second-stage fine-tuning (p. 4-7).
data_channel: Own dataset of 100,000 samples from the 3GPP TR 38.901 indoor factory channel model; also the public OPPO indoor-office dataset with 64 transmit beams (p. 8, 11).
test_conditions: 80/10/10 train, validation, test split of one dataset; probing size K fixed; models trained at one noise level also tested at other levels (p. 4, 8, 13).
baselines: Non-learned: largest-RSRP probing pair and hierarchical codebook search. Learned: FC, CNN, and VGG-BMNet [27] beam predictors, with regular probing patterns (p. 9, 13).
metrics: Top-Q beam prediction accuracy, marginal accuracy in dB, RSRP-difference CDF, top-1 throughput ratio, parameters, FLOPs, beam search time (p. 8-13).
complexity: Proposed predictor: 219,368 parameters and 1,004,288 FLOPs, versus VGG 3,107,456 and 20,596,736; CPU inference under 0.1 ms per sample (p. 12, 13, Tables VII, VIII).
openness: none released by the paper; uses the public OPPO dataset [31], https://wireless-intelligence.com/ (p. 11, 15).
q1_support: p. 8: "we adopt the parameters settings and modeling procedures specified by the 3GPP standard for an indoor mmWave channel (referred to as Indoor Factory (INF) channel)"; reference [30] (p. 15) is 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 13: "models trained on fixed noise level only exhibit better performance in the corresponding noise condition": the only train/test mismatch is the noise level, an SNR variation. Other results use one dataset with an 80/10/10 split (p. 8); no unseen scenario, band, or site is tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "Baseline scheme: A non-ML method which predicts the beam pair with the largest RSRP among the probing beam pairs" (non-learned); p. 9: "VGG-based scheme [27]" described as "recognized as the state-of-the-art (SOTA) scheme for spatial beam prediction", plus FC and CNN schemes, compared on top-1 accuracy (Fig. 9, 10).
q4_support: p. 11: "compared to the SOTA scheme VGG, DeePP reduces the number of network parameters by over 90% and decreases floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 20 times"; Table VII (p. 12) lists 219368 parameters and 1004288 FLOPs for the proposed network.
q5_support: p. 11: "we assess DeePP performance using a publicly available dataset for an indoor office scenario [31]" (Tables V and VI); reference [31] (p. 15) gives the OPPO dataset link. The paper does not release its own code or its indoor factory dataset.
notes: PDF page 1 holds the title 'Integrated Probing-Beam Pattern Learning and Beam Prediction for mmWave Massive MIMO' and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3538838. Area 3 because the output is an optimal beam-pair index (beam selection), not a channel. Borderline q2: Table IX trains models at one noise level and tests at the others, which I treated as an SNR sweep; the public-dataset experiment has its own 64-beam setup and is not a transfer test; the paper claims adaptation to various scenarios (p. 2) but does not test it. q5 rests on the public OPPO dataset [31]; whether that dataset is measured or simulated is not stated in the paper.
